question: What is the primary goal of the School Health Programme?

options.A: To replace primary health care clinics in rural communities
options.B: To ensure every child is healthy, well-nourished, and ready to learn
options.C: To generate revenue for the Ministry of Education
options.D: To provide advanced medical training for secondary school students

explanation: The overarching goal of the School Health Programme is to ensure that every child is healthy, well-nourished, and mentally alert to learn effectively. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is the school setting considered strategic for public health interventions according to the text?

options.A: Children spend a significant portion of their formative years there
options.B: Schools have unlimited budgets for healthcare delivery
options.C: Children do not get sick while inside a classroom
options.D: Teachers are legally qualified to perform minor surgeries

explanation: Because children spend a significant portion of their formative years in school, it serves as an ideal environment for public health interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes the scope of School Health Services?

options.A: Providing only emergency first aid for playground injuries
options.B: Screening, immunization, chronic condition management, and referrals
options.C: Conducting major surgical procedures for students
options.D: Administering academic examinations for health science students

explanation: School health services encompass routine health screening, immunizations, management of chronic conditions, first aid, and timely referrals. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of regular health assessments in the school setting?

options.A: Early detection of abnormalities that might impede learning
options.B: Immediate elimination of all communicable diseases in the country
options.C: Reduction of teachers' workload in the classroom

explanation: Regular health assessments help in the early detection of visual, auditory, and other abnormalities, which might otherwise impede learning if left unaddressed. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: What are the two main aspects of the school health environment?
explanation: The school health environment encompasses both the physical and psychosocial aspects of the school setting. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a physical environmental hazard that nurses should monitor?

options.B: Bullying among senior and junior students
options.C: Unsafe water supply and improper waste management

explanation: The physical environment includes safe water supply and proper waste management systems to prevent conditions like waterborne diseases. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of health education and instruction in schools?

options.A: To train students to become professional nurses and doctors
options.B: To translate health knowledge into practical, lifelong behaviors
options.C: To replace formal academic subjects with medical training
options.D: To diagnose student illnesses during classroom hours

explanation: Health education translates health knowledge into practical, lifelong behaviors and empowers students to make healthy lifestyle choices. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: How do school nurses typically contribute to health education and instruction?

options.A: By serving as resource persons, guest lecturers, or curriculum advisors
options.B: By grading mathematics and English assignments
options.D: By punishing students who break school health rules

explanation: Nurses often serve as resource persons, guest lecturers, or curriculum advisors, ensuring scientifically accurate information. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is the school-community partnership essential for the School Health Programme?

options.A: Communities provide financial profits to school administrators
options.B: Health goals require collaboration to reinforce health messages at home
options.C: Communities take over all teaching responsibilities from teachers
options.D: Schools are legally required to operate independent of parents

explanation: When parents and communities are engaged, health messages taught in school are reinforced at home, creating continuity in health practices. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which local bodies are specifically mentioned as vital structures for initiating and sustaining school health projects?

options.A: Parent-Teacher Associations and School-Based Management Committees

explanation: PTAs and SBMCs are vital structures through which health projects can be initiated and sustained. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is one of the primary benefits of school feeding programs in developing settings?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any other school health service
options.B: Incentivizing school enrollment and attendance while providing balanced meals
options.C: Training students to become professional food caterers
options.D: Generating surplus income for the school board

explanation: School feeding programs serve as a crucial safety net, incentivizing enrollment and attendance while providing a balanced meal. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: How do school nurses typically participate in nutrition and feeding services?

options.A: By cooking meals for the entire student body daily
options.B: By monitoring nutritional status and inspecting food vendors for hygiene
options.C: By importing foreign dietary supplements for all students
options.D: By setting the market prices for food items in the community

explanation: Nurses monitor nutritional status through anthropometric measurements and inspect school canteens and food vendors for hygiene standards. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What physiological benefit is associated with regular physical activity in school children?

options.A: Decreased need for sleep and rest periods
options.B: Strengthening of cardiovascular and musculoskeletal systems
options.C: Immediate immunity against all infectious diseases

explanation: Regular physical activity strengthens cardiovascular and musculoskeletal systems and combats childhood obesity. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is a key responsibility of the school nurse regarding physical education and recreation?

options.A: Serving as the permanent coach for the school football team
options.B: Ensuring equipment safety, proper field maintenance, and providing first aid
options.C: Grading students on their athletic performance and speed
options.D: Banning rough sports entirely from the school curriculum

explanation: School nurses ensure playground equipment is safe, fields are maintained, and provide immediate first aid for sports injuries. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is staff health and welfare considered essential to the School Health Programme?

options.A: Staff members pay the salaries of the school nurses
options.B: Staff well-being directly influences the quality of education and student safety
options.C: Staff members are legally classified as medical personnel
options.D: It prevents students from ever falling sick in school

explanation: Staff well-being directly influences the quality of education, classroom management, and the overall safety of students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h8)

question: Which of the following represents a common occupational hazard faced by school teachers?

options.A: Exposure to radiation from medical X-ray machines
options.B: Voice strain and ergonomic issues from prolonged standing
options.C: Injuries from operating heavy industrial machinery
options.D: Chemical burns from chemistry laboratory acids

explanation: Teachers face occupational hazards such as voice strain and ergonomic issues from standing for long hours. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in the School Health Programme?

options.A: Monitoring is ongoing data collection, while evaluation is periodic assessment of overall impact
options.B: Monitoring is done by students, while evaluation is done strictly by government officials
options.C: Monitoring focuses only on finances, while evaluation focuses only on academics
options.D: Monitoring happens after the school closes, while evaluation happens during exams

explanation: Monitoring involves ongoing data collection of daily activities, while evaluation is the periodic assessment of overall program impact against objectives. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h9)

question: How do nurses utilize the evidence gathered from monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: To penalize students with poor health records
options.B: To identify gaps, justify interventions, and ensure continuous quality improvement
options.C: To replace the school curriculum with nursing textbooks
options.D: To determine the school fees for the following academic session

explanation: Evidence gathered helps identify gaps, strengths, and justifies necessary interventions to ensure continuous quality improvement. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h9)
